book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 2 Structure, VCP Squeeze & Support Shelves
question: What does the multi-timeframe 1W/1D/4H tape tell us about institutional accumulation, volatility contraction, and the exact no-FOMO entry shelf?

epigraph.quote: Fundamentals tell you what to buy; the multi-timeframe tape tells you when institutional hands are quietly absorbing supply—and where your thesis is wrong.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein & Mark Minervini Synthesis

web_blocks.html: As of November 13, 2026, Yash Highvoltage (BSE:YASHHV) sits in a confirmed Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend [19][24]. It is in Week 35 of Stage 2 with a +178.59% cumulative gain and a +157.44% 1-year return [19][24]. The stock rallied +75.25% over 6 months and +34.87% over 3 months to a 52-week high of ₹1,310.00 (low ₹366.00) [19]. Over the past month, it digested gains constructively (+2.98% 1M, -0.33% 1W) [19]. It closed Friday at ₹1,240.85 (-2.46% on the day), 5.28% below its 52-week high [19].

All three timeframes show an established uptrend, though extended weekly momentum demands entry discipline [19][24]. On the Weekly (1W) chart, price sits +32.63% above its 30-week SMA (₹935.58) and +8.42% above its 10-week EMA (₹1,144.46) [19]. Weekly RSI(14) is elevated at 75.20 while price sits +54.67% above its 200-day SMA (₹802.27) [19]. On the Daily (1D) chart, the TradingView daily feed shows RSI(14) 53.14, 50D SMA ₹1,138.18, and ATR(14) ₹61.28, versus the deterministic ledger feed (RSI 53.72, 50D SMA ₹1,133.10, ATR ₹62.01) [19][24]. On the 4-Hour (4H) chart, RSI(14) sits at 48.46 below the 4H 20-EMA (₹1,245.04) and near the 4H 50-SMA (₹1,224.87), signaling a pullback with no turn yet (intraday_4h_turn: false) [24].

Daily ATR(14) is ₹61.28 on TradingView (₹62.01 on the deterministic ledger) [19][24]. Friday's -2.46% dip traded 126,750 shares, matching the 30-day average of 124,025 shares (1.02x) with no institutional dumping [19]. Yash's Relative Strength (RS) outperforms the Nifty 50 by 15.44% [24]. However, broader market distribution is elevated (dist_days_25: 6, or 6 distribution days in the last 25 sessions).

Shareholding data confirms institutional support. The June 2026 preferential issue anchored Mutual Funds (2.45%) and AIFs (7.23%) alongside 53.79% unpledged promoter equity [6]. Note that YASHHV is not in the NSE F&O segment and has no liquid options chain [24]. All exposure must use cash equity [24]. That avoids expiry whipsaws, though it leaves cash-equity stop discipline as the sole risk tool [24].

The 4H chart has not turned up yet (4H RSI 48.46, below 4H 20-EMA ₹1,245.04), and Weekly RSI sits at 75.20 (+54.67% above the 200D SMA ₹802.27) [19][24]. Disciplined capital waits for price to meet rising support [24]. Our entry zone spans Pivot S1 (₹1,084.67) up to the 50-day SMA (₹1,138.18 TV / ₹1,133.10 ledger) and 10-week EMA (₹1,144.46) [19][24]. Together they form a clean ₹1,085–₹1,145 support zone, 7.7% to 12.6% below Friday's close [19][24]. Our hard stop at ₹990 sits above Pivot S2 (₹962.33) and above the 30-week SMA (₹935.58) [19][24]. That placement guards against a failed VCP while allowing normal small-cap volatility.

web_blocks.title: 8.4 Market Regime Context, Liquidity & Execution Checklist

web_blocks.html: Broader market and sector breadth demand caution. On November 13, 2026, the Nifty 50 logs 6 distribution days in the last 25 sessions (dist_days_25: 6). More importantly, sector breadth has diverged sharply: 3 of 4 listed T&D peers (VOLTAMP, CGPOWER, and APARINDS) trade below both their 50-day and 30-week SMAs in STAGE_4 / corrective action [21][22][23]. YASHHV (+15.44% RS) is the lone outlier holding Stage 2, which raises pullback risk if sector selling widens [19][24].

BSE liquidity supports retail and HNI sizing, averaging 124,025 shares/day (~₹15.4 crore daily turnover at ₹1,240.85) [19]. Still, Daily ATR(14) is ₹61.28 on TradingView (₹62.01 on the ledger), so midday market orders risk 1%–1.5% slippage. Always place limit orders inside the ₹1,085–₹1,145 support zone. Avoid placing stops on round numbers near stop clusters; our ₹990 stop sits cleanly near Pivot S2 (₹962.33) and the 30-week SMA (₹935.58) [24].

book_paragraphs: Once we know what a business is worth, we turn to the tape. Think of fundamental analysis as checking the structural integrity of a bridge, and technical analysis as checking the traffic and weather before you drive across it. On November 13, 2026, Yash Highvoltage closed at ₹1,240.85, down 2.46% on the day, sitting in Week 35 of a textbook Stan Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend.

Over the past year, the stock has risen 157.44%, climbing from a 52-week low of ₹366 to a high of ₹1,310. When a stock moves that far, novices assume it is too late, while gamblers chase every green candle. Neither approach works. You and I read the three-timeframe tape—Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour—to see whether institutions are distributing shares or quietly tightening supply.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Three Timeframes: 1W, 1D, and 4H
paragraphs: Start with the Weekly chart. Yash is trading 32.6% above its rising 30-week moving average at ₹935.58, 41.1% above its 40-week EMA at ₹879.28, and 8.4% above its 10-week exponential moving average at ₹1,144.46. Weekly RSI stands at 75.20, and price sits +54.67% above the 200-day SMA (₹802.27)—meaning long-term momentum is powerful, though extended. Now zoom into the Daily chart: the TradingView daily feed shows RSI(14) at 53.14, 50-day SMA at ₹1,138.18, and ATR(14) at ₹61.28, whereas the deterministic ledger feed logs RSI at 53.72, 50-day SMA at ₹1,133.10, and ATR at ₹62.01.

Finally, check the 4-Hour chart for immediate timing. Friday's 2.46% dip pushed 4-Hour RSI down to 48.46, right below the 4-Hour 20-EMA at ₹1,245.04 and resting near the 4-Hour 50-SMA at ₹1,224.87. Volume on the dip was 126,750 shares—virtually identical to the 30-day average of 124,025 shares. There is no panic selling here, just normal profit-taking inside a tight consolidation.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: When Weekly RSI sits at 75.20 and price is +54.67% above the 200-day moving average, patience is your greatest edge: let price come down to the ₹1,085–₹1,145 support zone rather than chasing.

book_subsections.title: The Volatility Contraction Squeeze and Institutional Sponsorship
paragraphs: Notice what is happening to volatility underneath the surface. Bollinger bandwidth has compressed to just 13.48%, with the stock hovering just 5.28% below its ₹1,310 all-time high, while Daily ATR sits at ₹61.28 on TradingView (₹62.01 on the deterministic ledger). In Mark Minervini's framework, this is a classic Volatility Contraction Pattern—a coiled spring where weak hands have already exited and institutional sponsors are holding firm.

We can verify that sponsorship directly from the September 2026 shareholding pattern. Mutual Funds hold 2.45% and Alternative Investment Funds hold 7.23% following the June 2026 preferential issue, while promoters hold 53.79% with zero shares pledged. Meanwhile, Yash's relative strength outperforms the Nifty 50 by 15.44% even though broader market distribution is elevated at 6 distribution days in the last 25 sessions. Even more telling, 3 of 4 listed T&D peers—Voltamp, CG Power, and APAR Industries—are trading below their 50-day and 30-week moving averages in Stage 4 corrective action.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash-Equity Discipline Matters Without Listed Options
paragraphs: Because Yash is not in the NSE F&O segment, there are no listed options to structure a collar or call spread. Every rupee of exposure must be managed in cash equity. On one hand, that protects the stock from monthly expiry pinning and derivatives-driven whipsaws. On the other hand, it means your only risk-management tool is your entry price and your hard stop.

Rather than buying blindly at ₹1,240.85 into a cooling 4-Hour tape where the intraday turn has not yet triggered, you and I map our buy zone to the institutional support shelf at ₹1,085 to ₹1,145—spanning Pivot S1 (₹1,084.67) up to the 50-day SMA (₹1,138.18 TV / ₹1,133.10 ledger) and 10-week EMA (₹1,144.46)—with a hard invalidation stop at ₹990 cleanly above Pivot S2 (₹962.33) and the 30-week SMA (₹935.58). If the stock instead breaks out above ₹1,310 on 1.5x average volume before pulling back, we demand volume confirmation rather than chasing thin air.

book_subsections.title: Mapping Every Price Level From Resistance to Invalidation
paragraphs: To execute cleanly without staring at intraday ticks, keep four exact price markers in front of you. Overhead resistance sits at the 52-week high of ₹1,310.00 and Pivot R1 at ₹1,319.67. Short-term equilibrium sits between the 20-day SMA at ₹1,230.47 and the 10-day SMA at ₹1,249.83. Our primary support shelf runs from ₹1,085 to ₹1,145, anchored by Pivot S1 at ₹1,084.67, the 50-day SMA (₹1,138.18 TV / ₹1,133.10 ledger), and the 10-week EMA at ₹1,144.46. Finally, our structural invalidation stop sits at ₹990, safely above Pivot S2 at ₹962.33 and the 30-week SMA at ₹935.58.

book_subsections.title: Sector Breadth Divergence and Distribution Headwinds
paragraphs: A stock never trades in a vacuum; it swims in the current of the broader market regime. As of November 13, 2026, the Nifty 50 has logged 6 distribution days in the last 25 sessions (dist_days_25: 6), signaling heavier institutional supply under the surface.

Sector breadth has also diverged sharply: 3 of 4 listed T&D peers—Voltamp Transformers, CG Power, and APAR Industries—have slipped below both their 50-day and 30-week moving averages into Stage 4 or corrective action. While Yash Highvoltage has outperformed the Nifty 50 by 15.44% in relative strength, buying an extended leader at 60x earnings while its sector peers correct invites unnecessary drawdown risk. Waiting for ₹1,085 to ₹1,145 respects both the stock's trend and the sector's caution flag.

book_subsections.title: Execution Mechanics: Limit Orders, Slippage, and Stop Placement
paragraphs: Because Yash Highvoltage trades on the BSE with a 30-day average volume of 124,025 shares—roughly ₹15.4 crore of daily turnover at ₹1,240.85—execution hygiene matters. A stock with a ₹61.28 daily Average True Range on TradingView (₹62.01 on the ledger, nearly 5% of its share price) can swing ₹25 to ₹35 intraday on modest order flow. Never use market orders in a ₹3,710 crore small-cap industrial.

Instead, let the market come to you with resting limit orders staged across ₹1,085 to ₹1,145. That zone spans Pivot S1 at ₹1,084.67 up to the 50-day SMA (₹1,138.18) and 10-week EMA (₹1,144.46). Meanwhile, our ₹990 hard stop sits safely below Pivot S1 and near Pivot S2 (₹962.33), ensuring ordinary intraday volatility does not shake you out prematurely while capping downside at ₹155 per share from the top of the entry zone.

book_subsections.title: Reading Volume Clues Inside a 35-Week Stage 2 Advance
paragraphs: Let us pause on one more technical clue that separates institutional accumulation from retail blow-offs: volume behavior during pullbacks. Over the past 35 weeks of Stage 2, Yash Highvoltage has climbed 178.59%, yet the stock never went parabolic on frantic retail turnover. Look at the past month: while the stock drifted sideways just 5.28% below its ₹1,310 peak, Bollinger bandwidth tightened to 13.48%.

On Friday, November 13, when the stock fell 2.46% to ₹1,240.85, total volume was 126,750 shares—virtually identical to the 30-day average of 124,025 shares. When a stock that is up 157.44% over twelve months pulls back on 1.02x average volume rather than 2.5x or 3x distribution volume, it tells you that the institutional funds who bought the June 2026 preferential issue are sitting tight on their shares. All that remains for us is to wait patiently for the 4-Hour chart to finish cooling into the ₹1,085 to ₹1,145 support shelf.

book_subsections.title: How to Tell a Healthy Consolidation From a Stage 3 Top
paragraphs: Every experienced trend follower eventually learns to ask: how do I know this sideways pause near ₹1,240.85 is a Stage 2 Volatility Contraction Pattern rather than the start of a Stage 3 distribution top? You look at three objective clues on the chart.

First, the 30-week moving average at ₹935.58 and the 50-day moving average at ₹1,138.18 (₹1,133.10 ledger) are both sloping steadily upward, whereas Stage 3 tops flatten out. Second, pullbacks are occurring on average volume—126,750 shares on Friday versus a 124,025-share 30-day average—rather than heavy institutional churning. Third, price remains within 5.28% of its 52-week high while Bollinger bandwidth contracts to 13.48%. Until Pivot S1 (₹1,084.67) and the ₹990 stop break decisively, the benefit of the doubt stays with the Stage 2 uptrend.
